chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id from Ya'qub ibn Yaqtin said:

I asked a virtuous man, peace be upon him, about a man who prays on a cloudy day not facing the qibla, then the sun rises while he is still within the prayer time. Does he repeat the prayer if he had prayed not facing the qibla, even if he had exerted himself to determine the qibla? Will his prayer suffice? He said: 'He repeats [the prayer] if it was within the time; and if the time has passed, there is no repetition for him.'

key_terms.اَلْقِبْلَة: The direction of prayer (towards the Kaaba in Mecca)
key_terms.تَحَرَّى: To seek/exert effort to find or determine
key_terms.يَوْمِ سَحَابٍ: A cloudy day (obscuring the sun/stars for direction finding)
key_terms.يُعِيدُ: He repeats (referring to repeating the prayer)

ai.seo_question: Does a Muslim need to repeat their prayer if they prayed facing the wrong direction due to clouds but within the correct time?
ai.summary: This ruling from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the principle of *ikhtiar* (due diligence) in determining the qibla, establishing that error during the active prayer window necessitates repetition (*i'adah*), whereas error persisting until the time expires does not. It highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the validity of the prayer act itself being contingent upon the correct orientation at the moment of performance, reflecting the broader legal theory of *khata'* (mistake) in ritual acts.
